name: Geotechnical Engineering II
description: Site characterization and field tests (SPT, CPT, plate load, pile load); types, selection, and design of foundations. Bearing capacity of shallow foundations using Terzaghi’s and Meyerhof’s theories, and deep foundations through pile analysis, load tests, group efficiency, and lateral response. Settlement analysis covering stress distribution, immediate and consolidation settlements. Slope stability of infinite and finite slopes using Swedish circle and related methods. Earth pressure theories of Rankine and Coulomb, retaining walls, and reinforced soil walls. Earth dams and embankments: design, seepage, and stability. Ground improvement through stabilization, anchorage, grouting, and geosynthetics. Introduction to earthquake geotechnics, liquefaction, seismic stability, machine foundations, geohazards, environmental geotechnics, sustainability, and underground structures.
